title: AstraZeneca inks $1.5B insitro deal for AI-enabled target discovery of liver, heart disease drugs
source_used: Analytics Insight (Fierce Biotech page blocked, HTTP 403)
key_facts: AstraZeneca signed a multi-year deal with AI biotech insitro, announced 15 Oct 2026
AstraZeneca pays USD 40 million upfront; insitro could get up to USD 1.46 billion in development and commercial milestones plus royalties
Focus is MASH (a serious liver disease) and cardiomyopathies (heart muscle diseases)
Insitro's Virtual Human platform combines lab-grown cell models with machine learning to find drug targets
Insitro works on targets nominated by AstraZeneca up to the development-candidate stage
AstraZeneca funds and runs later clinical trials and holds exclusive worldwide rights to selected programs
Insitro also works with Bristol Myers Squibb (ALS) and Eli Lilly
quote_evidence: Under the agreement announced on Thursday (October 15, 2026), AstraZeneca will pay insitro USD 40 million upfront.
The company could also receive up to USD 1.46 billion in development and commercial milestone payments, along with royalties from future sales of medicines developed through the collaboration.
Still, the agreement's commercial value will depend on research progress and achievement of specified milestones.
why_it_matters_hint: The headline $1.5 billion is mostly conditional milestone money; only $40 million is paid up front, and any drug still needs testing.
notes: Original Fierce Biotech page blocked; read Analytics Insight. Search results from AllSci and Euronext also show the USD 40 million upfront figure.
